paragraphs.key_phrase: chlorophyll, water and no true roots
paragraphs.meaning: Algae are photosynthetic organisms with a simple body called a thallus and no true roots, stems or leaves. They are grouped by pigment into green, brown and red algae. Their reproduction can be vegetative by fragmentation, asexual by spores, or sexual with gametes, and the group matters beyond botany: agar, carrageenan and much of the oxygen in the atmosphere come from them.

words.meaning: A plant body not differentiated into root, stem and leaf.
words.breakdown: Algae and bryophytes have a thallus; higher plants do not.
words.trap: A thallus is not a primitive root. It is an undivided body that does the whole job of the plant.

words.meaning: A gel extracted from red algae, used in culture media and food.
words.breakdown: It is obtained from genera such as Gelidium and Gracilaria.
words.trap: Agar comes from red algae, and algin from brown algae. The two are different products.

words.meaning: Sexual reproduction with gametes that look alike.
words.breakdown: Anisogamy has unlike gametes, and oogamy has a large non-motile egg and a small motile sperm.
words.trap: Isogamy does not mean the gametes are identical in behaviour. They may differ in mating type even when they look the same.

paragraphs.hook: The oxygen in your next breath may have been made by a single-celled alga in the sea.
paragraphs.exam_note: Match pigments and storage products: green algae have chlorophyll a and b with starch, brown algae have fucoxanthin with laminarin, red algae have phycoerythrin with floridean starch.
paragraphs.trap: Blue-green algae are not algae. They are cyanobacteria, prokaryotes, and belong to Monera.

recall.why: Agar is extracted from red algae such as Gelidium and Gracilaria, while brown algae give algin.

recall.q: The plant body of an alga is called a
recall.why: Algal bodies are undifferentiated thalli, without true roots, stems or leaves.

paragraphs.meaning: Bryophytes are the amphibians of the plant kingdom: they live on land but need water for their sperm to swim to the egg. The green leafy plant is the gametophyte, and the sporophyte grows out of it and depends on it. Mosses, liverworts and hornworts belong here, and peat moss is harvested on a scale that matters for fuel, soil and carbon storage.

words.meaning: The haploid generation that produces gametes.
words.breakdown: In bryophytes it is the green leafy plant; in ferns and seed plants the sporophyte dominates.
words.trap: The gametophyte is not a gamete. It is a whole plant generation that makes gametes.

words.meaning: The diploid generation that produces spores by meiosis.
words.breakdown: In a moss it is the stalked capsule growing from the leafy shoot.
words.trap: In bryophytes the sporophyte is attached to and fed by the gametophyte. It is not an independent plant.

words.meaning: Partly decayed moss remains, mainly from Sphagnum, used as fuel and soil conditioner.
words.breakdown: Peat bogs store large amounts of carbon.
words.trap: Peat is not soil. It is accumulated plant material in waterlogged, oxygen-poor conditions.

paragraphs.hook: A moss cannot reproduce in dry air, which is why it waits for rain.
paragraphs.exam_note: Bryophytes are tested on the dominant generation, the need for water, and the examples: Funaria and Sphagnum are mosses, Marchantia is a liverwort.
paragraphs.trap: Bryophytes have no vascular tissue, so they cannot grow tall. Their small size is not a stage of growth.

recall.q: In bryophytes the dominant generation is the
recall.why: The green leafy plant is the gametophyte, and the sporophyte is attached to it and dependent on it.

recall.q: Bryophytes are called amphibians of the plant kingdom because
recall.why: They live on land but their motile sperm must swim through water to reach the egg.

paragraphs.meaning: Pteridophytes are the first plants with vascular tissue, which is what lets them grow taller than mosses. The leafy fern is the sporophyte, and the gametophyte is a small separate prothallus. Spores form in sporangia, often in clusters called sori on the underside of fronds, and a few genera such as Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spore, a step towards the seed habit.

words.meaning: A cluster of sporangia on the underside of a fern frond.
words.breakdown: Sori appear as brown dots or lines under the leaflets.
words.trap: A sorus is not a seed or a fungus. It is a group of spore cases belonging to the fern.

words.meaning: Producing two kinds of spores, microspores and megaspores.
words.breakdown: Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous; most ferns are homosporous.
words.trap: Heterospory is not the same as having two sexes in one plant. It is two spore types, which later development separates into male and female gametophytes.

words.meaning: The small, free-living gametophyte of a fern.
words.breakdown: It grows from a spore and bears the sex organs.
words.trap: The prothallus is not a young fern. It is a separate haploid generation that the fern sporophyte grows out of.

paragraphs.hook: The brown dots under a fern leaf are not disease. They are the next generation being packed.
paragraphs.exam_note: Pteridophytes are tested on vascular tissue, the dominant sporophyte, sori and the heterosporous examples Selaginella and Salvinia.
paragraphs.trap: Ferns do not produce seeds. The seed habit appears later, in gymnosperms.

recall.q: Sori on a fern frond contain
recall.why: A sorus is a cluster of sporangia, and each sporangium produces spores by meiosis.
These two pteridophytes produce microspores and megaspores, unlike the homosporous ferns.

paragraphs.key_phrase: seeds enclosed in flowers and fruit
paragraphs.meaning: Gymnosperms bear naked seeds on cones, while angiosperms bear seeds inside an ovary that becomes a fruit. Gymnosperm reproduction is slow and the male gametes are carried by pollen tubes, so water is no longer needed for fertilisation. Angiosperms add double fertilisation, where one sperm fuses with the egg and another with two polar nuclei, forming the triploid endosperm that feeds the seed.

words.meaning: A seed not enclosed in an ovary or fruit.
words.breakdown: Cycas and Pinus bear seeds on the scales of cones.
words.trap: Naked does not mean unprotected. Gymnosperm seeds have coats; they simply lack an ovary around them.

words.meaning: The fusion of one sperm with the egg and another with two polar nuclei.
words.breakdown: It produces a diploid zygote and a triploid primary endosperm nucleus.
words.trap: Double fertilisation is not two eggs being fertilised. One fusion makes the embryo, the other makes the food store.

words.meaning: The nutrient tissue that feeds the developing embryo.
words.breakdown: In angiosperms it is usually triploid, formed after double fertilisation.
words.trap: Endosperm is not the same as the cotyledon. Both store food, but the endosperm is a separate tissue formed from the second fusion.

paragraphs.hook: A cone and an apple are two answers to the same problem: how to protect and feed a seed.
paragraphs.exam_note: Double fertilisation and the triploid endosperm are reliable one-mark answers, along with the examples Cycas and Pinus for gymnosperms.
paragraphs.trap: Gymnosperms do not have double fertilisation. It is a defining feature of angiosperms.

recall.q: Double fertilisation produces a zygote and
recall.why: One sperm fuses with the egg to make the diploid zygote, and the other fuses with two polar nuclei to make the triploid endosperm nucleus.

recall.q: Gymnosperm seeds are called naked because they
options: Are not enclosed in an ovary
recall.why: They sit on the scales of cones rather than inside an ovary, though they still have their own seed coats.
